chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from one of our companions, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The chief of the foods is the meat.
ai.seo_question: What is considered the best or chief food according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) identifies meat as the 'master of food' (Sayyid al-Ta'am), a title reflecting its superior nutritional density and status as a luxury item in the pre-modern Arabian context. This narration is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for establishing the merit of meat consumption, particularly during times of need or celebration, while scholars note it does not negate the virtue of other foods but rather highlights meat's unique role in strengthening the body for worship.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The chief of the foods is the meat’.
